conventions.convention: Paths are continuous maps [0,1] → U with a finite smooth subdivision. Thin homotopies fix endpoints and are smooth, with differential rank at most one, on a finite subdivision into the specified curvilinear triangles.
δ*γ traverses γ first and δ second; groupoid composition is [δ]∘[γ]=[δ*γ]. This differs from the traversal-first fundamental-group product used by the CW supplier.
Transport solves U′=−ω(γ̇)U with U(0)=I₄; later path segments multiply on the left. The tetrad application inherits ACω.
The inherited coframe convention is e′=Λe, E′=EΛ⁻¹ and ω′=ΛωΛ⁻¹−dΛΛ⁻¹; curvature is F=dω+ω∧ω. Local frame changes are principal-bundle gauge transformations only with the stated global extension.

The small square traverses +eᵢ,+eⱼ,−eᵢ,−eⱼ, positively oriented for (eᵢ,eⱼ). Its transport has quadratic term −ε²Fᵢⱼ. Matrix size q and coordinate dimension n are independent, and the remainder is uniform over the specified compact K.

The finite graph includes both orientations through a fixed-point-free reversal involution. Reverse labels are inverses, path holonomy is later-left ordered, empty holonomy is I₂, and vertex gauge action is g′ₑ=hₜ₍ₑ₎gₑhₛ₍ₑ₎⁻¹.

Vertex averaging assumes full AC and normalized Haar probability. Vertex factors contain every incoming Vₑ and outgoing Vₑ*, in fixed orders; empty tensor products are ℂ. Representations assigned to reverse orientations need not be related.

load_bearing.statement: Piecewise-smooth paths have finite smooth partitions; a thin homotopy is continuous, fixes endpoints, and has rank at most one on each smooth curvilinear triangle of a finite subdivision.
For the local tetrad Lorentz connection, assuming the supplier's ACω convention, connection path transport is the endpoint of the unique continuous piecewise-C¹ solution U′γ=−ω(γ̇)Uγ, Uγ(0)=I₄.

For a finite connected CW complex K, a vertex v₀ and a maximal tree T, π₁(K,v₀) has generators the oriented non-tree edge loops and relators the based 2-cell attaching words. Cells of dimension at least three add no generators or relators.
Thin homotopy is an equivalence relation on paths with fixed endpoints and respects concatenation. Tagged classes, constant paths and reversed paths give a groupoid with composition [δ]∘[γ]=[δ*γ].
Under the assumptions of connection path transport, thin-homotopic piecewise-smooth paths have equal endpoint transport matrices in the fixed tetrad trivialization.

A finite SU(2) graph configuration assigns inverse matrices to reverse edges, uses later-left path products, and transforms by g′ₑ=hₜ₍ₑ₎gₑhₛ₍ₑ₎⁻¹. Wilson traces use strongly continuous finite-dimensional unitary representations.

Assuming full AC, normalized Haar averaging of the stated finite-dimensional vertex representation is the orthogonal projection onto its fixed-vector subspace. The vertex-factor projections commute and their product projects onto the joint invariant subspace.

concerns.concern: The Definition uses “a piecewise-smooth path γ:[0,1]→U”, whose exact convention is supplied by def-gr-fx-thin-paths, but that item is absent from deps and Definition references. The earlier page placement supplies the reader's meaning, so this is a dependency declaration omission rather than a false transport claim.
